proofs.proof_tex:
For a panel law \(P\), Definition \texttt{def:target} gives, at every query where the relevant regular conditional expectations exist,
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]-
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]\right\}.                     \tag{1}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, after its stated definition of \(\mu_s(z_0)\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]=\mu_s(z_0)
 \quad\text{for every }i                                      \tag{2}
\]
outside a marginally null set.  Thus the treated observed mean in the claimed formula does not depend on the chosen replica.  Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency} is an almost-sure equality, so disintegration gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]
 =\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]                 \tag{3}
\]
outside another marginally null set.  Assumption \texttt{ass:event-date-transport} gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]=m_s(z_{0s})                  \tag{4}
\]
outside a marginally null set.  There are finitely many cohorts and replicas at each triangular-array index.  Intersecting the conull sets for (2)--(4) and substituting (3)--(4) into (1) proves the first display for marginal-almost-every \(z_0\).

Now fix an admissible query and a labelled causal kernel
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Equation (2) in Definition
\texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} states for every replica that
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\mu_s.       \tag{5}
\]
Its consistency clause and (5) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}(1)=\mu_s,                  \tag{6}
\]
while its transport clause implies
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_{0s}).            \tag{7}
\]
Applying Definition \texttt{def:target} to this fixed-query causal extension and substituting (6)--(7) gives
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}.       \tag{8}
\]
The right side of (8) is \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\) by Definition \texttt{def:fixed-query-functional}.  Thus consistency and event-date transport prove the relationship between the observed-law functional and the causal contrast; the relationship is not created by definition.  No density, temporal-mixing, donor, rank, inversion, or division condition is used.

Put \(q=Sd\) and
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda.    \tag{1}
\]
Every \(n_s\) and \(\pi_s\) is positive, so \(A>0\) and every later division by \(\sqrt A\) is valid.
We first work in the deterministic experiment
\(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\).  Here \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) are fixed known specifications: the infimum ranges over rules that may depend on them but are chosen before the unknown labelled point \(\xi=(\mathbb Q_\xi;\mu,f,z)\).  This timing is different from the outer generated-query frontier considered later.

Conditional on the donor sample define
\[
 U_{si}=E_{si}-\mu_s-K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \{Q_{s,t_{s\ell},i}-f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})\}.                 \tag{2}
\]
The donor sample is independent of all unit histories, and the histories are independent across \((s,i)\).  Thus the variables in (2) are conditionally centered and independent across \((s,i)\).  Boundedness gives \(|U_{si}|\le4B\), whence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\!\left(
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}U_{si}
 \mathrel{\Big|}(Z_j)_j\right)\le16B^2A.                    \tag{3}
\]

Let \(t_s^0\) be the smallest nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\).  The definition of \(t_{s\ell}\) and two triangle inequalities give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|X_{s,t_{s\ell}}-z_s\|_2
 &\le \|X_{s,t_s^0}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2
       +\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2\\
 &\le \rho_{sX}(z_{0s})+\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2
       +2\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2.
\end{aligned}                                                  \tag{4}
\]
Because \(0<\lambda\le1\), the map \(x\mapsto x^\lambda\) is subadditive.  Holder continuity and (4) yield
\[
 |f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})-f_s(z_s)|
 \le C\{\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda+
 \|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda+
 \|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2^\lambda\}.                \tag{5}
\]
Projection onto the cube is nonexpansive, every balanced donor fold has cardinality at least \(N/3\), and \(\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)\le qC_\Sigma\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\|\widetilde z_\ell-z\|_2^2
 \le\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}{|I_\ell|}
 \le\frac{3qC_\Sigma}{N}.                                   \tag{6}
\]
The experiment also imposes \(\|z-z_0\|_2^2\le C_\Sigma/N\).  Expanding \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\) into the centered sum in (3) and the approximation terms in (5), applying Jensen's inequality to (6), and then using \((x+y+z)^2\le3(x^2+y^2+z^2)\), gives
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \le C\{A+D_X^2+N^{-\lambda}\}.                            \tag{7}
\]
The nearest-site estimator is measurable in the observed array and the known fixed specifications, and it does not use \((\mu,f,z)\).  It is therefore an admissible witness for the first minimax inequality.  When \(\delta_0<1/2\), Lemma \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} makes the right side of (7) at most \(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\).

We next prove the deterministic converse.  If two laws \(P_0,P_1\) have targets separated by \(\Delta\) and total variation at most \(1-\eta\), let \(A_0=\{|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0|<\Delta/2\}\).  On \(A_0\) the error under law one is at least \(\Delta/2\), and on \(A_0^c\) the error under law zero is at least \(\Delta/2\).  Hence
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v(\widetilde\theta-\theta_v)^2
 \ge\frac{\Delta^2}{8}\{P_0(A_0^c)+P_1(A_0)\}
 \ge\frac{\eta\Delta^2}{8}.                                 \tag{8}
\]

For the treated-mean channel, take \(f_s=0\), deterministic \(Q_{sti}=0\), and \(z=z_0\), and keep these coordinates and the donor law fixed.  Under \(v\in\{-1,1\}\), take the \(E_{si}\)'s independent with values in \(\{-b,b\}\), where \(0<b<B\), and
\[
 \Pr_v(E_{si}=b)=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,
 \qquad \varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.      \tag{9}
\]
Because \(A\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), sufficiently small fixed \(\gamma\) places every probability in \([1/4,3/4]\).  The mean is the same for every replica in cohort \(s\), as required by the experiment.  The target separation is \(4\gamma\sqrt A\).  The Hellinger affinity of the two product event laws is
\[
 \prod_{s=1}^{S}(1-4\varepsilon_s^2)^{n_s/2}
 \ge\exp(-C\gamma^2/b^2)>0,                                  \tag{10}
\]
because \(\sum_sn_s\varepsilon_s^2=\gamma^2/b^2\).  If \(a_H\) is this affinity, Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le(1-a_H^2)^{1/2}<1\).  Thus (8) yields risk at least \(cA\).  A common admissible donor law for the prescribed \(\Sigma\) is supplied by the zero-displacement member of Lemma \texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair}; the strict fourth-moment slack assumed for the converse guarantees its membership.

For the fixed-design channel define
\[
 q_s(x)=a_0\min_{1\le t\le T}\|x-X_{st}\|_2^\lambda,
\]
with \(a_0>0\) small in terms of \(B,L,d\), and take \(f_s=q_s/2\), \(g_s=-q_s/2\).  Lemma \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} proves that these surfaces are admissible and agree at every design site.  Deterministic zero responses, identical event laws, and identical donors therefore give identical observations, while the targets differ by \(a_0D_X\).  Equation (8) with \(\eta=1\) yields risk at least \(cD_X^2\).

For the donor channel apply Lemma \texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} under strict interior and fourth-moment slack, choosing its nonzero coordinate in a cohort \(s_0\).  Under both laws use the common surface
\[
 f_{s_0}(x)=a_1|x_k-z_{0,s_0k}|^\lambda,
 \qquad f_s(x)=0\quad(s\ne s_0),                              \tag{11}
\]
with \(a_1\) small enough for the Holder and boundedness restrictions.  Keep response and event laws identical.  If \(e\) is the displaced coordinate, the construction in that lemma and ellipticity give
\[
 |z_{1,e}-z_{0,e}|
 =\frac{c_\eta N^{-1/2}}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}
 \ge c_\eta c_\Sigma^{1/2}N^{-1/2}.                          \tag{12}
\]
The donor products have total variation at most \(1-\eta\), while (11)--(12) separate their targets by at least \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\).  Equation (8) yields risk at least \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Taking the maximum of the three lower bounds and using Lemma \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} proves
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \ge cR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}.                                    \tag{13}
\]

We now pass to a fixed-query kernel.  Fix admissible \(z_0\) and
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  By Definition \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}, conditional on the exact design, donors are independent of the unit histories, histories are independent across \((s,i)\), and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[Q_{sti}\mid\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]=\mu_s
                                                                    \tag{14}
\]
for every replica.  The common value in (14) is the fixed-query implementation of Assumption \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}.  Consequently, for \(\mathbb K_\xi\)-almost every exact design, the conditional observed law with labels is the central point \(z=z_0\) of \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\).  Bounded responses give \(|m_s(X_{st})|\le B\) almost surely; the density lower bound makes this true Lebesgue-almost everywhere, and Holder continuity extends it to all \(x\in[0,1]^d\).  Thus \(\|m_s\|_\infty\le B\), as required by that experiment.  Its target is
\[
 \theta_{\mathfrak E}
 =\sum_s\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0).                             \tag{15}
\]
Applying (7) conditionally proves the nearest-design bound.  If each design contains \(z_{0s}\), then \(D_X=0\), and the exact-site conclusions follow from the geometry lemma.

Suppose instead that \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every \(s\).  Then \((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) is feasible in every foldwise anchor search.  Certificate optimality gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &C_H\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s\widehat h_{s\ell}^d)^{-1/2}\\
 &\quad\le C_H\|z_{0s}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +C_V\{Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d\}^{-1/2}.
\end{aligned}                                                   \tag{16}
\]
The bandwidth floor makes the last term no larger than a constant times \((h_s^\star)^\lambda\).  At every selected regular-branch pair, \(\lambda_{\min}(G_{sT})\ge c_G>0\), so the local fit is invertible.  Since \(r=0\), its intercept has nonnegative weights summing to one.  Because each response average is already in \([-B,B]\), its convex combination is in \([-B,B]\), so the formal clipping in Definition \texttt{def:frontier-estimator} is inactive.  Holder continuity bounds approximation bias by the first two terms on the left of (16), while conditional independence of whole unit histories and (14) bound the centered variance by \(CA\).  Donor unbiasedness, projection contraction, and
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^2\le3qC_\Sigma/N
\]
follow as in (6).  Jensen's inequality and (16) now yield
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2
 \mid(X_{st})]\le CR_D.                                      \tag{17}
\]
The geometry lemma gives \(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D\).

Finally, let \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  Lemma \texttt{lem:panel-fixed-query-kernel-transfer} gives a labelled point in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), with the common cohort treated mean required in (14), for marginal-almost-every admissible query.  Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} gives \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau(z_0)\) on the same conull set.  Equations (15)--(17) therefore transfer to the causal conditional kernel for almost every query and, after conditioning, almost every exact design.  The deterministic subexperiment allowed dependence on known \(X,z_0,\Sigma\); the feasible outer estimators \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}\) and \(\widehat\tau\) themselves use only the observable data and fixed sample-size constants and do not reveal the unknown donor mean \(z_0\).  No regular conditional version is selected at a query-null value.

Write
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad D_T=\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d}. \tag{1}
\]
Positivity of the cohort weights and replication counts gives \(A>0\), so the treated-pair normalization by \(\sqrt A\) below is well defined.
Fix \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}\) and
\(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  The estimator in Definition \texttt{def:frontier-estimator} is one \(\mathcal O\)-measurable rule formed from donor means and the observed panel; it neither receives \(z_0\) nor reads a nuisance label.  Thus it is selected before the unknown donor mean \(z_0\) and the labelled kernel, as required in the outer frontier.

Let \(\mathcal G=\{g_{sT}(z_0)<1\text{ for every }s\}\).  On \(\mathcal G\), Theorem \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} gives the conditional risk bound \(CR_D\).  Both \(\widehat\tau\) and \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}\) lie in \([-2B,2B]\), so squared error is at most \(16B^2\) on \(\mathcal G^c\).  Since \(0<h_s^\star\le1\),
\[
 \Pr_{\mathbb K_\xi}(\mathcal G^c)
 \le\sum_s\Pr_{\mathbb K_\xi}(h_s^\star=1)
 \le\sum_s\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}. \tag{2}
\]
The bandwidth floor gives
\[
 \{Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d\}^{-1/2}\le(h_s^\star)^\lambda,        \tag{3}
\]
because \((h_s^\star)^{2\lambda+d}\ge(Tn_s)^{-1}\).  Apply Lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} to (2)--(3), then Cauchy--Schwarz and Minkowski to the weighted sum of \((h_s^\star)^\lambda\).  Uniformly over the fixed query and labelled point,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2]
 \le C\bigg[&A+
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2\\
 &+D_T+N^{-\lambda}\bigg]
 \le CR_\star.                                                \tag{4}
\end{aligned}
\]
This calculation uses only query-conditional design mixing for anchor occupancy.  Sampling fluctuation was already controlled across complete independent unit histories, and no response-calendar mixing has been introduced.

The displayed smoothing component is redundant.  Set \(a_s=n_s^{-1/2}\) and \(b=T^{-\lambda/d}\).  Direct exponent arithmetic gives
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =a_s^{2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}b^{d/(2\lambda+d)}
 \le a_s\vee b.                                               \tag{5}
\]
Since \(S\) is fixed, Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2
 \le2S\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}+2T^{-2\lambda/d}
 \le C(A+D_T).                                                 \tag{6}
\]

For the converse, if two laws \(P_0,P_1\) have target separation \(\Delta\) and total variation at most \(1-\eta\), the event
\(A_0=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_0|<\Delta/2\}\) gives
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v(\widetilde\tau-\theta_v)^2
 \ge\eta\Delta^2/8.                                         \tag{7}
\]
Indeed, on \(A_0\) the law-one error is at least \(\Delta/2\), on \(A_0^c\) the law-zero error is at least \(\Delta/2\), and
\(P_0(A_0^c)+P_1(A_0)\ge1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\ge\eta\).

Under \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\), embed a treated-mean pair at \(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf1\).  Choose \(0<b<c\) with \(c+b<B\), use independent uniform exact designs, set every untreated regression and deterministic training response equal to \(c\), and use a common admissible donor law.  Under \(v\in\{-1,1\}\), let the observed treated wealth be independent across replicas and take values \(c-b,c+b\) with
\[
 \Pr_v(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=c+b)=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,
 \qquad \varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.       \tag{8}
\]
The distribution is identical across replicas within a cohort, so its conditional mean is common, while no equality of full distributions is required by the class.  Small fixed \(\gamma\) makes the probabilities admissible.  The target separation is \(4\gamma\sqrt A\), and the product Hellinger affinity is bounded away from zero because
\(\sum_sn_s\varepsilon_s^2=\gamma^2/b^2\).  Cauchy--Schwarz then bounds total variation away from one.  Set treated potential wealth equal to the observed coordinate and untreated event wealth equal to \(c\).  Baseline wealth one, horizon-zero return equal to wealth minus one, and later returns zero verify Definition \texttt{def:buyhold-level}.  Equation (7) yields \(cA\).

Lemma \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} supplies two degenerate-query panel laws and corresponding labelled points at different admissible fixed queries.  Because the outer infimum is over one rule chosen before the query, the lemma and (7) yield \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies two labelled points in one fixed-query class with a common submeasure bounded away from zero and separation of order \(D_T^{1/2}\), yielding \(cD_T\).  Combining these three subexperiments with (6) proves
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2]
 \asymp A\vee D_T\vee N^{-\lambda}\asymp R_\star.           \tag{9}
\]

On the independent-calendar subclass, Lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} replaces \(D_T\) in (4) by \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  For the reverse inequality use i.i.d. uniform design and a cube of radius \(r_T=cT^{-1/d}\) around \(z_{01}\).  Let
\[
 \phi(u)=\prod_{k=1}^{d}\psi(u_k),
 \qquad
 \psi(v)=
 \begin{cases}
  \exp\{1-(1-v^2)^{-1}\},&|v|<1,\\
 0,&|v|\ge1.
 \end{cases}
\]
Take one surface constant and the other equal to it plus
\(ar_T^\lambda\phi((x-z_{01})/r_T)\), with fixed \(a>0\) small enough for the Holder and support bounds.  They agree outside the cube and differ at its center by \(ar_T^\lambda\).  If \(v_d\) is a dimensional volume constant, then sufficiently small fixed \(c\) gives
\[
 \Pr\{X_{1t}\text{ misses the cube for every }t\}
 \ge(1-v_dr_T^d)^T\ge c_2>0.                                 \tag{10}
\]
On this event the two observed laws coincide, while their targets differ by \(c_1T^{-\lambda/d}\).  Equation (7) gives the lower squared-risk term \(cT^{-2\lambda/d}\).

For \(S=1\), \(H=0\), \(p=d=1\), and \(n_1=n\), (4) has the unreduced bookkeeping scale
\[
 n^{-1}\vee(Tn)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+1)}
 \vee T^{-2\lambda}\vee N^{-\lambda}.
\]
Equation (6) shows that the second term is dominated by the maximum of the first and third.  Finally, Lemma \texttt{lem:panel-fixed-query-kernel-transfer} supplies each panel law's labelled fixed-query point, including its common treated mean, for marginal-almost-every query, and Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} identifies its observed-law target with \(\tau(z_0)\).  Applying (4) on that conull set proves the causal transfer without evaluating a null conditional version.

Fix \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}\) and a labelled point
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Boundedness gives
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\in[-2B,2B]\).  On the regular branch, \(r=0\) and selected Gram coercivity gives \(\lambda_{\min}(G_{sT})\ge c_G>0\), so each local fit is invertible.  Its local-constant intercept has nonnegative weights summing to one.  Since every response average is in \([-B,B]\), the intercept already lies in \([-B,B]\), so clipping is inactive.  Conditional on the exact design and donor sample, the selected weights are response-independent.  Define one variable per complete unit history by
\[
 \zeta_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\left[
 B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s
 -\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_{st}\{Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\}\right].         \tag{1}
\]
Donor--panel independence means that conditioning additionally on donors does not change the conditional unit-history law given the design.  The common treated conditional mean and training centering in Assumption \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, as implemented by Definition \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}, center (1) for every replica.  Conditional cross-unit independence makes the variables independent across \((s,i)\).  No within-unit training/event independence is used.  Their range lengths are at most
\[
 d_{si}=\frac{2B\pi_s}{n_s}
 \left(1+\sum_{t=1}^{T}|w_{st}|\right).                       \tag{2}
\]
For \(V\in[a,b]\), convexity of the exponential gives
\(\mathbb E\exp\{u(V-\mathbb EV)\}\le
\exp\{u^2(b-a)^2/8\}\).  Multiplication over the independent histories, exponential Markov, optimization over \(u>0\), and a union bound over the two tails yield
\[
 \Pr_{\mathbb K_\xi}\left\{
 \left|\sum_{s,i}\zeta_{si}\right|>r_{\mathrm{unit}}
 \mathrel{\Big|}\mathcal X,(Z_j)_j\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}.                                   \tag{3}
\]
The positive linear term in \(r_{\mathrm{unit}}\) only enlarges the radius.  This argument treats each whole unit history as one bounded variable and uses no calendar-score independence.

Put \(q=Sd\).  Spectral clipping gives
\(\widehat\Sigma\succeq(c_\Sigma/2)I_q\).  Every donor fold has size at least \(N/3\), so donor unbiasedness and
\(\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_q\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\left[
 N\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2^2\right]
 \le\frac{6qC_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma}.                             \tag{4}
\]
This uses only the deterministic lower eigenvalue after clipping and does not require independence of the sample mean and covariance estimate.  Markov's inequality, a union bound over at most two folds, and the definition of \(q_{\mathrm{don}}\) imply
\[
 \Pr_{\mathbb K_\xi}\left\{
 \max_\ell\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}
 (\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2>q_{\mathrm{don}}N^{-1/2}\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.                                  \tag{5}
\]
On the complement, \(\widehat\Sigma\preceq2C_\Sigma I_q\), and projection onto the cube is nonexpansive relative to \(z_0\).  Hence
\[
 \max_\ell\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2
 \le (2C_\Sigma)^{1/2}q_{\mathrm{don}}N^{-1/2}.              \tag{6}
\]

At a selected local-constant fit, nonnegative unit-mass weights and kernel support give
\[
 \left|\sum_tw_{st}^{(\ell)}m_s(X_{st})
       -m_s(\widetilde z_{\ell s})\right|
 \le C\{\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
          +\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda\}.                     \tag{7}
\]
Holder continuity from \(\widetilde z_{\ell s}\) to \(z_{0s}\), (6), and the defining domination by \(C_H\) bound deterministic error by
\(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Combining (3), (5), and
\(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha\) proves coverage on the regular branch.  Every declared bad branch returns \([-2B,2B]\), which contains the target, and intersecting a covering interval with this known range preserves coverage.  Thus coverage is at least \(1-\alpha\) whenever the regular construction is used and is one on a bad branch; the stated uniform asymptotic coverage follows.

For expected length, \(\sum_t|w_{st}|=1\) on the regular branch.  Therefore, with \(A=\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\),
\[
 r_{\mathrm{samp}}=r_{\mathrm{unit}}
 \le C(\alpha,B)A^{1/2},                                      \tag{8}
\]
where \(\max_s\pi_s/n_s\le A^{1/2}\).  Let
\(\mathcal G=\{h_s^\star<1\text{ for every }s\}\).  On \(\mathcal G\), certificate optimality at \((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) and the bandwidth floor imply
\[
 r_{\mathrm{bias}}
 \le C\sum_s\pi_s\left\{(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\right\}.             \tag{9}
\]
Donor unbiasedness, ellipticity, projection contraction, and Jensen's inequality give
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\le CN^{-\lambda/2}.   \tag{10}
\]
The interval length is always at most \(4B\), and
\[
 \Pr_{\mathbb K_\xi}(\mathcal G^c)
 \le\sum_s\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}. \tag{11}
\]
Applying Lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} to (9)--(11) yields, uniformly over fixed queries and labelled points,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)
 \le C\bigg[&A^{1/2}
 +\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\\
 &+\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{\lambda/d}
 +N^{-\lambda/2}\bigg]+CR_\star.                             \tag{12}
\end{aligned}
\]
All inputs are finite under boundedness; searches are compact or finite with deterministic fallbacks, and spectral clipping is total.  Along the stated growth arrays the branches \(N<2\) and \(n_s<2\) eventually disappear.  The final term in (12) charges the full interval on \(\mathcal G^c\).  Since \(R_\star\to0\), eventually \(R_\star\le R_\star^{1/2}\).  The smoothing domination proved in Theorem \texttt{thm:marginal-phase-diagram} therefore gives
\[
 \sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)
 \le CR_\star^{1/2}.                                         \tag{13}
\]
In the independent-calendar subclass, the anchor lemma replaces the logarithmic term by \(T^{-\lambda/d}\).

For the converse, suppose two observed laws with targets \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) have a common subprobability measure \(\nu\) of mass \(\eta>2\alpha\).  Uniform coverage \(1-\alpha-o(1)\) under both laws gives
\[
 \nu\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I_\alpha\}
 \ge\eta-2\alpha-o(1).                                      \tag{14}
\]
Every interval on this event has length at least \(|\theta_1-\theta_0|\); hence
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)
 \ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\{\eta-2\alpha-o(1)\}.              \tag{15}
\]
For any pair \(P_0,P_1\), take \(\vartheta=P_0+P_1\) and define
\(d\nu=\min\{dP_0/d\vartheta,dP_1/d\vartheta\}\,d\vartheta\).  Then \(\nu\le P_0,P_1\) and
\(\nu(\mathcal O)=1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\), proving the common-measure claim used in (14).

The treated pair from the marginal proof has a cohort-common treated mean and can have overlap arbitrarily close to one by reducing \(\gamma\); it yields \(cA^{1/2}\).  For the donor channel apply Lemma \texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} with \(\eta\in(2\alpha,1)\).  Use a common independent uniform design and, in the displaced cohort, the common regression
\[
 m(x)=b_0+a_0|x_k-z_k^{(0)}|^\lambda,                          \tag{16}
\]
with constant regressions elsewhere, deterministic responses
\(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})\), a common positive treated wealth for every replica, and untreated event wealth \(m_s(z_s^{(v)})\) under alternative \(v\).  Small \(a_0,b_0\) verify support and Holder smoothness.  The panel coordinates coincide, the donor laws have common mass at least \(\eta\), and ellipticity converts the Mahalanobis displacement into coordinate separation at least \(cN^{-1/2}\).  Thus (16) separates the targets by at least \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\), and (15) yields the donor lower bound.

Lemma \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies in one fixed-query class a common mass exceeding \(2\alpha\) and target separation
\(c\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{\lambda/d}\).  Equation (15), followed by smoothing domination, yields \(cR_\star^{1/2}\).  In the independent-calendar class, choose the no-hit cube in the marginal proof small enough that its common mass exceeds \(2\alpha\); this yields \(cT^{-\lambda/d}\).  These pairs prove the uniformly honest expected-length converse for every one \(\mathcal O\)-measurable interval selected before the unknown \(z_0\) and \(\xi\).  This outer timing is essential to the donor lower bound and differs from the known-specification convention in \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\).

Finally, Lemma \texttt{lem:panel-fixed-query-kernel-transfer} places every panel law's labelled regular conditional point, with its common treated mean, in the fixed-query class for marginal-almost-every query.  Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} gives \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau\) there.  Applying (3)--(13) on that conull set proves causal coverage and expected-length transfer and makes no assertion at a query-null value.

Put \(q=Sd\) and \(\Delta_B=B^4-q^2>0\).  Choose \(a_D>1\) such that
\[
 1<a_D^2<1+\Delta_B/2.                                        \tag{1}
\]
For \(|u|\) in a sufficiently small fixed neighborhood of zero, define \(V_u\in\{-a_D,0,a_D\}\) by
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}+\frac{u}{2a_D},\quad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}-\frac{u}{2a_D},\quad
 p_0(u)=1-\frac{1+u^2}{a_D^2}.                                \tag{2}
\]
At zero the three probabilities are strictly positive, so they remain probabilities after shrinking the neighborhood.  Direct summation gives
\[
 \mathbb EV_u=u,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(V_u)=1.             \tag{3}
\]
Let \(R_2,\ldots,R_q\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of \(V_u\), and put
\(V_u^{(q)}=(V_u,R_2,\ldots,R_q)^\top\).  At \(u=0\),
\[
 \mathbb E\|V_0^{(q)}\|_2^4
 =a_D^2+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2=q^2-1+a_D^2<B^4.                       \tag{4}
\]
The centered fourth moment is continuous in \(u\), so the strict bound persists on a smaller fixed neighborhood.

Put \(z^{(0)}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_q\) and
\(z^{(1)}=z^{(0)}+\delta_Ne_1\), where
\(\delta_N=c_*N^{-1/2}\).  Since \(\delta_0<1/2\), both paths satisfy the interior restriction for all sufficiently large \(N\).  Under alternative \(v\in\{0,1\}\), take i.i.d. donors whose first coordinate is
\(1/2+V_{v\delta_N}\) and whose remaining coordinates are \(1/2\) plus the common Rademacher coordinates.  Equations (3)--(4) give
\[
 \mathbb E_vZ_j=z^{(v)},\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_v(Z_j)=I_q,
 \qquad \mathbb E_v\|Z_j-z^{(v)}\|_2^4\le B^4.              \tag{5}
\]
Because \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), this covariance is admissible.

The square roots of the three probabilities in (2) have bounded second derivatives near zero.  Their affinity is one at zero and has derivative
\(\tfrac12\sum_rp_r'(0)=0\).  Integrating the bounded second derivative twice gives a one-donor Hellinger affinity of at least \(1-C_0\delta_N^2\).  For densities \(p,g\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \frac12\int|p-g|
 \le\left\{1-\left(\int\sqrt{pg}\right)^2\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
Product factorization then yields
\[
 \|P_1^{Z,N}-P_0^{Z,N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\{1-(1-C_0\delta_N^2)^{2N}\}^{1/2}.                     \tag{6}
\]
Choosing fixed \(c_*>0\) sufficiently small makes (6) at most \(1-\eta_0\) for some fixed \(\eta_0>0\).

Use a common i.i.d. uniform exact training design.  If \(0<\kappa<1\), which here is equivalent to \(0<\lambda<1\), set
\[
 m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)_+^\kappa;
\]
if \(\kappa=1\), set
\[
 m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2).                                    \tag{7}
\]
Set every other surface equal to \(b_0\).  In the first case, subadditivity of the \(\kappa\)-power proves the required \(\lambda\)-Holder bound; in the second, the affine surface is Lipschitz.  Sufficiently small positive \(b_0,b_1\), depending only on \(B,L\), enforce the Holder radius and boundedness.  Moreover,
\[
 |m_1(z^{(1)}_1)-m_1(z^{(0)}_1)|
 =b_1\delta_N^\kappa.                                        \tag{8}
\]

Use identical bounded centered training noise, the same training design, and the same positive constant treated observation for every cohort and replica under both laws.  Hence the revised treated-mean replication condition holds, as does its invariance under further design conditioning.  Set
\(B_{si}(1)=B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and set the unobserved untreated event wealth to \(m_s(z_s^{(v)})\).  Taking \(W_{si,-1}=1\),
\(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\), and \(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\) realizes these wealth levels under Definition \texttt{def:buyhold-level}.

Conditional on either degenerate query, the uniform design has density one and beta-mixing coefficients zero.  The construction verifies boundedness, Holder smoothness, consistency, transport, and both clauses of design-conditional centering.  Histories are independent across \((s,i)\), with arbitrary dependence within a history allowed.  Donors are independent of the common panel, and (5) verifies donor independence, unbiasedness, ellipticity, and the fourth-moment bound.  Both laws therefore lie in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).

The observed panel factors are identical and (6) controls the only differing observed factor.  Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (8) give
\[
 |\tau_1(z^{(1)})-\tau_0(z^{(0)})|
 =\pi_1b_1c_*^\kappa N^{-\kappa/2}.                           \tag{9}
\]
This is the asserted explicit witness and does not assume a class-wide lower local modulus.

Put \(q=Sd\).  Since \(B^4\ge q^2\), the common donor law
\(Z_j=z_0+U_j\), with independent Rademacher coordinates in \(U_j\), has mean \(z_0\), covariance \(I_q\), and
\(\mathbb E\|U_j\|_2^4=q^2\).  Take it independent of the complete joint panel.

Choose \(\gamma>0\) so small that \(e^{-\gamma}>2\alpha\), and define
\[
 L_T=\left\lfloor
 \frac{\log T-2\log\log(T\vee3)}{|\log\rho_0|}
 \right\rfloor\vee1,
 \qquad p_T=\frac{\gamma L_T}{T}.                             \tag{1}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\),
\[
 2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}.                               \tag{2}
\]
Partition the first cohort's calendar into complete consecutive blocks of length \(L_T\).  Independently label each complete block by
\(C_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Let \(A_T\) be a cube centered at \(z_{01}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_d\) with volume \(p_T\).  Conditional on \(C_b=1\), draw all design points in the block independently uniformly on \(A_T\); conditional on \(C_b=0\), draw them independently uniformly on \(A_T^c\).  At every date in a complete block the marginal density equals
\[
 p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
 +(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1                 \tag{3}
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every \(x\).  Draw the incomplete block and all other cohorts independently and uniformly, so the fixed-query density bounds hold.

For a lag \(k<L_T\), past and future sigma-fields separated by \(k\) dates share at most one Bernoulli block label.  Couple one copy by replacing that shared label on the future side with an independent copy.  The mismatch probability is
\(2p_T(1-p_T)\le2p_T\), which bounds the absolute-regularity coefficient.  If \(k\ge L_T\), the sigma-fields use disjoint independent labels and the coefficient is zero.  Since \(\rho_0^k\ge\rho_0^{L_T-1}\) for \(k<L_T\), (2) gives
\[
 \beta(k)\le2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}
 \le\beta_0\rho_0^k.                                        \tag{4}
\]

Let \(E_T\) be the event that every complete-block label is zero and that no point in the incomplete block lies in a fixed smaller concentric cube.  The incomplete-block failure probability is at most \(L_Tp_T=o(1)\), whereas
\[
 \Pr(E_T)=(1-p_T)^{\lfloor T/L_T\rfloor}-o(1)
 \longrightarrow e^{-\gamma}>
 \eta_\alpha:=\frac{e^{-\gamma}+2\alpha}{2}>2\alpha.        \tag{5}
\]
Let \(h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}\) be the side scale of the smaller cube.  Define
\[
 \phi(u)=\prod_{k=1}^{d}\psi(u_k),\qquad
 \psi(v)=
 \begin{cases}
  \exp\{1-(1-v^2)^{-1}\},&|v|<1,\\
 0,&|v|\ge1.
 \end{cases}
\]
After a fixed rescaling its support lies in the smaller cube.  For sufficiently small fixed \(a,b_0>0\), put
\[
 m_{10}(x)=b_0,\qquad
 m_{11}(x)=b_0+ah_T^\lambda\phi((x-z_{01})/h_T),              \tag{6}
\]
and keep other surfaces equal to \(b_0\).  A derivative of order \(j\le\lfloor\lambda\rfloor\) of the perturbation is bounded by a constant times \(h_T^{\lambda-j}\), and its top-order Holder seminorm is uniformly bounded.  Thus fixed small \(a\) places both surfaces in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), and small \(a,b_0\) enforce boundedness.

Under alternative \(v\), set \(Q_{1ti}=m_{1v}(X_{1t})\), use the common constant surfaces elsewhere, and take the same positive constant treated observation for every replica.  The latter verifies common treated-mean replication and design invariance.  Impose consistency and set untreated event wealth equal to \(m_{sv}(z_{0s})\).  Baseline wealth one, horizon-zero return equal to wealth minus one, and later returns zero realize the buy-and-hold levels.  Conditional centering is exact; conditional on the design, histories are degenerate and hence mutually independent.  Equations (3)--(4) verify query-conditional design regularity, and the donors satisfy all donor conditions.  Both laws are in the panel class and their labelled kernels are in the same fixed-query class.

On \(E_T\), no response is evaluated in the bump support.  The restrictions of the two observed laws to \(E_T\) coincide, giving a common subprobability measure of mass at least \(\eta_\alpha\) for sufficiently large \(T\).  Finally, Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (6) yield
\[
 |\tau_1(z_0)-\tau_0(z_0)|
 =\pi_1ah_T^\lambda
 \asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}. \tag{7}
\]
This proves the required common-submeasure certificate.

Write
\[
 \rho_s=\rho_{sX}(z_{0s}),\qquad
 D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_s^\lambda,
 \qquad A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}.                 \tag{1}
\]
Take a feasible triple \((f,g,z)\) in Definition \texttt{def:joint-product-modulus} and put \(q_s=f_s-g_s\).  If \(t_s\) is a nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\), nonnegativity of every term in the response budget gives
\[
 |q_s(X_{st_s})|^2
 \le\sum_{t=1}^{T}|q_s(X_{st})|^2\le n_s^{-1}.               \tag{2}
\]
The difference of two members of \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) is \(\lambda\)-Holder with constant at most \(2L\).  Thus
\[
 |q_s(z_{0s})|\le n_s^{-1/2}+2L\rho_s^\lambda.               \tag{3}
\]
The donor budget and \(\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\) imply
\[
 \|z-z_0\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(z-z_0)\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}N^{-1/2}.                                 \tag{4}
\]
Split the functional difference at \(g_s(z_{0s})\).  Equations (3)--(4), Holder continuity, \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\), and
\(\sum_s\pi_sn_s^{-1/2}\le S^{1/2}A^{1/2}\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\mathcal T(f,z_0)-\mathcal T(g,z)|
 &\le\sum_s\pi_s|q_s(z_{0s})|
      +L\sum_s\pi_s\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda\\
 &\le C\{A^{1/2}+D_X+N^{-\lambda/2}\}.
\end{aligned}                                                  \tag{5}
\]
Taking the supremum proves the upper bound for \(\Omega_X\).  The same argument with one cohort and no donor displacement proves
\[
 \omega_{s,X}(1;z_{0s})
 \le n_s^{-1/2}+2L\rho_s^\lambda.                             \tag{6}
\]

For fixed-design lower bounds let
\(\mathcal X_s=\{X_{s1},\ldots,X_{sT}\}\) and define
\[
 q_s(x)=a\,\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal X_s)^\lambda,       \tag{7}
\]
where \(a>0\) is small enough in terms of \(B,L,d\).  Distance to a nonempty closed set is one-Lipschitz, and subadditivity of \(x^\lambda\) for \(0<\lambda\le1\) gives
\[
 |u^\lambda-v^\lambda|\le|u-v|^\lambda,
 \qquad u,v\ge0.                                              \tag{8}
\]
Hence \(f_s=q_s/2\) and \(g_s=-q_s/2\) belong to \(\mathcal F_{\lambda,L,B}\), agree at all design sites, and differ at \(z_{0s}\) by \(a\rho_s^\lambda\).  Taking \(z=z_0\) consumes zero testing budget.  Applying the construction in one cohort and then simultaneously in all cohorts proves
\[
 \omega_{s,X}(1;z_{0s})\ge a\rho_s^\lambda,
 \qquad \Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)\ge aD_X.                      \tag{9}
\]

Assume \(\delta_0<1/2\).  Choose a coordinate direction \(v\) pointing from the corresponding coordinate of \(z_0\) toward \(1/2\).  There is a constant
\[
 0<a_0\le\frac12\min\{c_\Sigma^{1/2},1/2-\delta_0\}
\]
such that \(u_N=a_0N^{-1/2}v\) keeps \(z_0+u_N\) in the \(\delta_0\)-trimmed cube and
\[
 N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2^2
 \le Nc_\Sigma^{-1}\|u_N\|_2^2\le1.                        \tag{10}
\]
In the affected cohort, a sufficiently small multiple of
\(x\mapsto\{v_s^\top(x-z_{0s})\}_+^\lambda\) lies in \(\mathcal F_{\lambda,L,B}\).  Use that same surface as both \(f_s\) and \(g_s\), zero surfaces elsewhere, and take \(z=z_0+u_N\).  The response budget is zero, while the functional separation is at least \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\), because the selected cohort weight is positive.  Therefore
\[
 \Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)\ge cN^{-\lambda/2}.                  \tag{11}
\]
Equations (5), (9), and (11), together with
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}=A\vee\Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)^2\), prove
\[
 R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\asymp A\vee D_X^2\vee N^{-\lambda}      \tag{12}
\]
under strict interior slack.  Without that slack, (5) still gives
\[
 R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}
 \le C\{A\vee D_X^2\vee N^{-\lambda}\}.                     \tag{13}
\]

Finally, suppose \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every \(s\).  Since \(r=0\), the Gram matrix is scalar.  Its strict positivity at \((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\), together with the support of \(K\), implies that at least one design point lies within \(h_s^\star\) of \(z_{0s}\); hence \(\rho_s\le h_s^\star\).  The bandwidth floor gives
\[
 \{Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d\}^{-1/2}\le(h_s^\star)^\lambda.       \tag{14}
\]
Substitute \(D_X\le\sum_s\pi_s(h_s^\star)^\lambda\), (14), and Definition \texttt{def:conditional-rate} into (13) to obtain
\[
 R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D.                                 \tag{15}
\]
No lower local-modulus condition was invoked.

Put \(q=Sd\).  Select a signed coordinate vector \(e\), with its sign pointing toward \(1/2\) in that coordinate, and set
\[
 w=\frac{\Sigma^{-1/2}e}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}.
\]
Let \(O\) be an orthogonal matrix sending the first standard basis vector to \(w\).  Because \(B^4>q^2\), choose
\(\epsilon\in(0,B^4-q^2)\) and put \(a=(1+\epsilon)^{1/2}>1\).  For \(u\) near zero define \(A_u\in\{-a,0,a\}\) by
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a^2}+\frac{u}{2a},\qquad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a^2}-\frac{u}{2a},\qquad
 p_0(u)=1-\frac{1+u^2}{a^2}.                                 \tag{1}
\]
At \(u=0\) all probabilities are strictly positive, so they remain probabilities for \(|u|\le u_0\), for some \(u_0>0\).  Direct summation gives
\[
 \mathbb EA_u=u,\qquad \mathbb EA_u^2=1+u^2,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}(A_u)=1.                           \tag{2}
\]
Let \(R_2,\ldots,R_q\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of \(A_u\), and define
\(V_u=O(A_u,R_2,\ldots,R_q)^\top\).  Then
\[
 \mathbb EV_u=uw,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(V_u)=I_q.         \tag{3}
\]
Orthogonal invariance and independence give
\[
 \mathbb E\|V_u-uw\|_2^4
 =\mathbb E(A_u-u)^4+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2.                          \tag{4}
\]
At \(u=0\), (4) equals
\(a^2+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2=q^2+\epsilon<B^4\).  It is continuous in \(u\), so, after reducing \(u_0\), it is at most \(B^4\) for \(|u|\le u_0\).

Let \(G_u\) be the law of
\[
 Z_u=z_0+\Sigma^{1/2}V_u.
\]
Equations (3)--(4) imply
\[
 z(u):=\mathbb EZ_u
 =z_0+u\Sigma^{1/2}w
 =z_0+\frac{u}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}e,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}(Z_u)=\Sigma,                      \tag{5}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_u-z(u))\|_2^4\le B^4.           \tag{6}
\]

The Hellinger affinity between \(G_0\) and \(G_u\) is
\[
 a_H(u)=\sum_{r\in\{-,0,+\}}\{p_r(0)p_r(u)\}^{1/2},         \tag{7}
\]
because all other finite-support coordinates have the same law.  The probabilities in (1) stay bounded away from zero near zero, so \(a_H\) has bounded second derivative there.  Moreover,
\(a_H(0)=1\) and \(a_H'(0)=\tfrac12\sum_rp_r'(0)=0\).  Integrating \(a_H''\) twice yields
\[
 a_H(u)\ge1-Cu^2.                                             \tag{8}
\]
For \(CNu^2\le1/2\), product factorization and
\(1-x\ge e^{-2x}\) for \(0\le x\le1/2\) give
\[
 a_H(u)^N\ge(1-Cu^2)^N\ge e^{-2CNu^2}.                       \tag{9}
\]
For dominated probability laws, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|P-G\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 &=\frac12\int|\sqrt p-\sqrt g|(\sqrt p+\sqrt g)\\
 &\le\left\{1-\left(\int\sqrt{pg}\right)^2\right\}^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}                                                  \tag{10}
\]
Choose \(c_\eta>0\) small enough that (9)--(10), with
\(u=c_\eta N^{-1/2}\), give total variation at most \(1-\eta\).  Reduce it further so that
\[
 c_\eta\le u_0\wedge1
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 c_\eta C_\Sigma^{1/2}\le\frac12-\delta_0.
\]
Equation (5) then gives
\[
 N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}\{z(c_\eta N^{-1/2})-z_0\}\|_2^2
 =c_\eta^2.                                                    \tag{11}
\]
By ellipticity,
\[
 \frac{c_\eta N^{-1/2}}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}
 \le c_\eta C_\Sigma^{1/2}.
\]
The coordinate displacement points toward \(1/2\), so the preceding choice keeps it in the \(\delta_0\)-trimmed cube for every \(N\ge1\).  Take \(G_0=G_{u=0}\), \(G_1=G_{u=c_\eta N^{-1/2}}\), and \(N_\eta=1\).  Equations (5)--(11) prove the claim for the prescribed full covariance.

proposed.condition:
With \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{1\le u\le S,\ 1\le v\le T})\), for every \(s,t,i\),
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{st}),
\]
and, on defining the cohort mean
\(\mu_s(z_0):=\mathbb E[B_{s1}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]\), every replica \(i\) satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]
 =\mu_s(z_0),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\mu_s(z_0)
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\]

standard.name: conditional mean centering for replicated random-design regression and panel sample means

proposed_core_edits.reason: The former condition allowed replica-specific treated means, so conditioning on the exact design did not yield the deterministic experiment's single cohort label.  The replacement adds only the intended common conditional mean and preserves unrestricted within-unit dependence.

proposed.name: Deterministic induced fixed-design product experiment
proposed.construction:
Fix a deterministic array \(X=(X_{st})_{1\le s\le S,1\le t\le T}\), an interior reference path \(z_0\), and \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S_{++}^{Sd}\).  The local deterministic product experiment \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) consists of labelled parameter points \(\xi=(\mathbb Q_\xi;\mu,f,z)\), where \(\mathbb Q_\xi\) is a law of
\[
 \mathcal O_X=\bigl((E_{si})_{s,i},(Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}\bigr)
\]
labelled by \((\mu,f,z)\), where \(\mu=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_S)\in[-B,B]^S\), every \(f_s\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) satisfies \(\|f_s\|_\infty\le B\), and
\[
 z\in([0,1]^d)^S,\qquad
 \operatorname{dist}(z_s,\partial[0,1]^d)\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(z-z_0)\|_2^2\le1.
\]
Under \(\mathbb Q_\xi\), \(|E_{si}|\vee|Q_{sti}|\le B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}E_{si}=\mu_s,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}Q_{sti}=f_s(X_{st}),
\]
the histories \(((E_{si},(Q_{sti})_{t=1}^{T}))_{s,i}\) are independent across \((s,i)\), with arbitrary dependence within a history, and the donor sample is independent of these histories and is i.i.d. with
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}Z_j=z,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb Q_\xi}(Z_j)=\Sigma,\qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z)\|_2^4\le B^4.
\]
The statistical target attached to \(\xi\) is
\[
 \theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)
 =\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mu_s-f_s(z_s)\}.
\]
The deterministic specifications \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) are known inputs to a decision rule in this experiment.  An estimator may depend on those specifications and on \(\mathcal O_X\), and it is selected only before the unknown labelled point \(\xi\); it may not inspect the labels \((\mu,f,z)\).  This is distinct from the outer generated-query fixed-kernel frontier, where a single \(\mathcal O\)-measurable rule is selected before the unknown donor mean \(z_0\) and the labelled kernel.  The deterministic experiment does not select a version of a regular conditional distribution at a null design.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), so \(\kappa=\lambda\),
\(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\), and fix the class constants.  For every deterministic
exact design \(X=(X_{st})\), every interior reference path \(z_0\), and
every \(c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\), consider
the deterministic experiment \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) in
\texttt{def:fixed-design-induced-experiment}.  Its nearest-design estimator
satisfies
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \left[\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2\right]
 \le
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \left[\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2\right]
 \le C\left\{\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
          \vee D_X(z_0)^2\vee N^{-\lambda}\right\}.
\]
If \(\delta_0<1/2\), the last display is at most
\(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)\).  If in addition
\(B^4>(Sd)^2\), then
\[
 cR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)
 \le
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \left[\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2\right].
\]
Neither bound uses a lower local-modulus condition.

For every fixed admissible \(z_0\) and every
\(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), the conditional law under
\(\mathbb K_\xi\) given the exact design, with its labels, belongs to
\(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) for \(\mathbb K_\xi\)-almost every design,
and \(\theta_{\mathfrak E}=\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\).  Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \left[\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}
 -\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2\mid(X_{st})\right]
 \le C\left\{\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
          \vee D_X(z_0)^2\vee N^{-\lambda}\right\}
\]
for almost every design; under \(\delta_0<1/2\), its right side is at most
\(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\).  If every cohort design contains \(z_{0s}\)
exactly, the displayed risk is at most
\(C\{\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\vee N^{-\lambda}\}\), and
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le C\{\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\vee N^{-\lambda}\}\).
If instead \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every cohort, then
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \left[\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2
 \mid(X_{st})\right]\le CR_D,
 \qquad R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D.
\]
No converse in terms of \(R_D\) is asserted.

For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), its labelled observed regular
conditional kernel belongs to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for
almost every admissible \(z_0\) under the marginal law of the query, and
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau(z_0)\) there by
\texttt{lem:causal-identification}.  Hence all preceding conditional upper
bounds transfer to \(P\) at those query values and at
\(P(\cdot\mid z_0)\)-almost every exact design; no conditional version at a
null query is selected.
proposed.justification: The deterministic subexperiment permits dependence on known \(X,z_0,\Sigma\), while its feasible nearest-site witness remains observable; the panel bridge now carries a common treated mean.
proposed.gap: Donoho's known Gaussian convex experiment and Akhavan et al.'s strong-convexity minimizer problem do not supply this bounded product law, external query geometry, or almost-everywhere causal bridge.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), so \(\kappa=\lambda\), and
\(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\).  Uniformly over fixed admissible query values and their
conditional-kernel classes, the anchor estimator obeys
\[
 \sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2]
 \le CR_\star.
\]
The estimator is a single data-measurable rule and does not use the query or
nuisance labels.  This upper bound uses no lower local-modulus condition.  If
\(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\), then, still over the base Holder class,
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}
 \sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2]
 \asymp R_\star
 \asymp
 \left\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}\right\}
 \vee\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{2\lambda/d}
 \vee N^{-\lambda},
\]
where the infimum is over one data-measurable rule chosen before both
suprema.  Thus the nonredundant oracle/generated-proxy boundary is
\[
 N^{-\lambda}\asymp
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\right\}
 \vee\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}.
\]
The smoothing component in \(R_{\mathrm{or}}\) is algebraically dominated
for fixed \(S\) and is not a fourth nonredundant phase.  On the fixed-query
independent-calendar subclasses, both spacing displays replace the
logarithmic term by \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  In the scalar specialization
\(S=1\), \(H=0\), \(p=d=1\), and \(n_1=n\), the unreduced bookkeeping form is
\[
 n^{-1}\vee(Tn)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+1)}
 \vee T^{-2\lambda}\vee N^{-\lambda},
\]
and its second term is dominated by the maximum of the first and third.

Separately, for every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), its labelled
regular conditional kernel belongs to
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for almost every query under the marginal
law of \(z_0\).  At each such query,
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau(z_0)\) and the displayed upper-risk conclusion
applies to \(P(\cdot\mid z_0)\).  No supremum over \(P\)-specific null
conditional values is asserted.
proposed.justification: One \(\mathcal O\)-measurable anchor rule chosen before the query and label attains the treated-replication, conditional-spacing, and donor-location maximum under the repaired transfer.
proposed.gap: Geometric conditional design mixing incurs the logarithmic spacing term; conditional design independence removes it, while higher smoothness remains outside the theorem.
proposed.consumer: Applications can locate the oracle/generated-proxy boundary without an oracle label, a lower local modulus, or a null regular-conditional version.

Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), so \(\kappa=\lambda\),
\(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\).  Along every growth array with
\(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), the total interval \(C_\alpha\)
in \texttt{def:honest-interval} satisfies
\[
 \liminf
 \inf_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}

 \Pr_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \{\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\in C_\alpha\}
 \ge1-\alpha,

and
\[
 \sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)]
 \le CR_\star^{1/2}.
\]
These conclusions use no lower local-modulus condition, count the full-range
interval on every declared bad-sample branch, and never divide by an
estimated variance.  If \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\), every single
data-measurable random interval \(I_\alpha\) having the same uniform
fixed-query-kernel coverage obeys
\[
 \sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)]
 \ge cR_\star^{1/2}
\]
for all sufficiently large indices.  On the fixed-query
independent-calendar subclasses, both upper and lower spacing terms are
\(T^{-\lambda/d}\).  The theorem makes no higher-order claim for
\(\lambda>1\).

For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), its labelled regular
conditional kernel is in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for almost
every query under the marginal law of \(z_0\), and
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau(z_0)\) there.  Therefore the coverage and

prose_updates.tldr: The paper delivers the rough-Holder frontier for \(0<\lambda\le1\). A repaired sampling condition makes each cohort's treated conditional mean common across replicas while leaving their distributions and within-unit training/event dependence unrestricted. The deterministic fixed-design experiment treats \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) as known specifications, whereas every outer generated-query estimator and interval is one observable rule chosen before the unknown donor mean; this distinction preserves the \(N^{-\lambda}\) phase. At each admissible query, uniform random-design statements are over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), and a disintegration lemma transfers them to each panel law only for almost every query. The nonredundant channels are treated replication, query-conditional calendar spacing, and full-covariance donor location; the feasible interval concentrates whole unit histories and has no calendar-score branch.

project_justification.gap: Classical fixed-point regression does not combine replicated sites with an external full-covariance generated query, and the former panel-to-kernel argument did not ensure that every treated replica shared the deterministic experiment's cohort mean. A panel regular conditional law is also not defined canonically at query-null values.
project_justification.niche: Historical paths are observed exactly while only the event query is synthesized. The repaired common-mean condition closes the treated-replica transfer without imposing identical distributions, within-unit training/event independence, or response-calendar mixing. Known-specification fixed-design recovery and unknown-query outer decision theory are kept distinct.
project_justification.fill: The note proves conditional, marginal, and honest-length rate frontiers for \(0<\lambda\le1\). A nearest-site rule attains the deterministic fixed-design scale when \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) are known specifications; an anchor/extrapolation rule and a total interval remain single observable procedures chosen before the unknown donor mean. Explicit treated, spacing, and full-covariance donor pairs match the upper rates, and a common-mean disintegration lemma supplies the causal panel bridge almost everywhere in the query.

sampling_model.design: At a fixed admissible query, each exact-design coordinate has conditional density between \(c_X\) and \(C_X\) almost everywhere and each cohort's design sequence is geometrically beta mixing. The independent-calendar subclass imposes conditional independence only on design dates. These conditions transfer from a joint panel law only on a marginal-conull set of queries.
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated blocks and \(n_s\) treated event outcomes. Conditional on the exact design, unit histories are independent across replicas. Their training responses have mean \(m_s(X_{st})\), and every treated replica has the same cohort mean \(\mu_s(z_0)\), invariant under further design conditioning. Full distributions may differ across replicas, and dependence across training dates and the event within one unit remains unrestricted.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency identifies observed event wealth with treated potential wealth. The repaired replication clause makes its conditional mean common within cohort. Event-date transport separately equates the unobserved untreated event mean with the historical regression at the realized path; neither centering nor query overlap proves that causal equality.
sampling_model.overlap: Every admitted query is at least \(\delta_0\) from the cube boundary. The donor-location converse uses strict slack \(\delta_0<1/2\); exact fixed-design recovery can be easier when a design site equals the query.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the event query is generated. Donor folds provide projected means and the full stacked covariance retains all cross-coordinate, cross-horizon, and cross-cohort entries. For \(0<\lambda\le1\), local-constant weights are nonnegative and have unit mass, so whole-unit bounded-range concentration suffices without response mixing, deconvolution, or calendar-score studentization.

prose_updates.related_work: Donoho (1994) studies a known Gaussian convex experiment; here the deterministic bounded product experiment instead has replicated responses, an external full-covariance location coordinate, and fixed specifications \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) known to its decision rule. Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) study independently estimated minimizers under strong convexity, where center error is second order rather than a rough-Holder modulus. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) provide ordered-modulus and bias-aware ordinary-regression interval benchmarks, while Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) study dependent synthetic-control prediction; none supplies an outer generated-query rule, common-treated-mean panel disintegration, or the donor expected-length converse proved here. Stone (1982), Fan (1993), Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012), Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008), Low (1997), and Ferman (2021) remain rate, generated-covariate, adaptation, and replication context rather than substitutes for the theorem.
prose_updates.interpretation: The repaired fixed-query class makes the cohort treated mean a genuine common label after exact-design conditioning. This is a mean restriction only: it does not homogenize replica distributions or break dependence within a unit history. Donor uncertainty dominates when \(N^{-\lambda}\) exceeds treated replication and conditional spacing. A deterministic optimal-recovery rule may use known \(X,z_0,\Sigma\); the outer feasible rule may not use \(z_0\), because it must learn that donor mean. Causal interpretation transfers only at almost every realized query.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Every constructive headline is restricted to \(0<\lambda\le1\) and fixed admissible queries; panel-law statements hold only almost everywhere in the query. The common treated-mean restriction is necessary for the present deterministic-experiment transfer but does not control conditional variances or higher moments beyond boundedness. For \(\lambda>1\), signed local-polynomial weights need additional stochastic stability. Geometric conditional design mixing retains the logarithmic spacing penalty, the donor converse requires \(B^4>(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0<1/2\), and exact phase-intersection constants remain open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Event-date transport remains untestable. The revised centering condition imposes a common treated conditional mean across replicas and invariance to the exact design, but no identical distributions, within-unit training/event independence, or response-calendar mixing. Fixed-design minimax rules know \(X,z_0,\Sigma\); outer risk and interval rules are chosen before the unknown \(z_0\) and label. The interval uses no calendar-score branch or estimated-variance division. Panel-law conclusions hold only on a marginal-conull query set; higher smoothness, growing dimension, adaptation, uniform-in-query bands, and exact constants remain outside scope.
