proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(z_0\) and
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  The bounded-wealth and consistency
clauses of Definition \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} imply
\(|B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}|\le B\) almost surely, so all expectations below
exist.  Its common-label and design-conditional-centering clauses give
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s\mid\mathcal X]=0.                 \tag{1}
\]
For bounded \(\mathcal X\)-measurable \(W\), the pull-out and tower
properties of conditional expectation yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s)W]
 &=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\!\left[
 W\,\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 (B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s\mid\mathcal X)\right]\\
 &=0.
 \end{aligned}                                                  \tag{2}
\]
This proves the asserted orthogonality.

Let \(E\in\mathcal X\) and set \(p_E=\mathbb K_\xi(E)\).  Taking
\(W=\mathbf 1_E\) in (2) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mathbf 1_E]=\mu_sp_E.                  \tag{3}
\]
If \(p_E>0\), division by \(p_E\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E]=\mu_s. \tag{4}
\]
Applying the same argument to \(E^c\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E^c]=\mu_s \tag{5}
\]
when \(p_E<1\).  Thus (4)--(5) hold simultaneously when
\(0<p_E<1\), and Lemma \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction}
supplies the stated exclusion.  By Lemma
\texttt{lem:panel-fixed-query-kernel-transfer}, every
\(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) induces a labelled point
\(\xi_P(z_0)\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for almost every query.
Applying (1)--(5) to those points proves the panel-to-kernel transfer and
makes no claim at a query-null version.

We now construct the two labelled points.  For arbitrary positive integers
\(N,T,n_1\), take
\[
 S=1,\quad \pi_1=1,\quad H=0,\quad p=d=1,\quad z_0=\frac12,
 \quad \lambda=\kappa=1,\quad B=L=1,\quad \delta_0=\frac14,   \tag{6}
\]
and set \(c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), with any fixed \(\beta_0>0\)
and \(\rho_0\in(0,1)\).  These values satisfy all declared parameter
ranges, and \(d=p(H+1)=1\).

On a product probability space let \((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T}\),
\((\eta_j)_{j=1}^{N}\), and \((\varepsilon_i)_{i=1}^{n_1}\) be mutually
independent, with
\[
 X_{1t}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[0,1],
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(\eta_j=1)=\mathbb P(\eta_j=-1)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(\varepsilon_i=1)=\mathbb P(\varepsilon_i=-1)=\frac12. \tag{7}
\]
Define
\[
 m_1(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Q_{1ti}=m_1(X_{1t})=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Z_j=\frac12+\eta_j.                                           \tag{8}
\]
For every event unit set \(W_{1i,-1}=1/2\) and \(R_{1i0}(0)=0\).
Definition \texttt{def:buyhold-level} then gives
\[
 B_{1i}(0)=\frac12.                                             \tag{9}
\]
Under \(\mathbb K_0\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=0\); under \(\mathbb K_1\), set
\(R_{1i0}(1)=\varepsilon_i/2\).  In each case impose consistency by setting
\(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{1i}(1)\).  Hence
\[
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\frac12\quad\text{under }\mathbb K_0,
 \qquad
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\frac12+\frac14\varepsilon_i
 \quad\text{under }\mathbb K_1.                               \tag{10}
\]
The smallest constructed return is \(-1/2>-1\), so the declared return
support is respected.

For \(r\in\{0,1\}\), give \(\mathbb K_r\) the labels
\[
 \mu_1=\mu_{11}(z_0)=\frac12,
 \qquad m_1(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad \Sigma=1,                                              \tag{11}
\]
and call the resulting point \(\xi^{(r)}\).  We verify membership.
Equations (8)--(10) imply
\[
 |Q_{1ti}|=\frac12,
 \qquad |B_{1i}(0)|=\frac12,
 \qquad |B_{1i}(1)|\le\frac34,                                \tag{12}
\]
so bounded wealth holds.  The constant \(m_1\) has supremum norm \(1/2\)
and zero Lipschitz seminorm, hence \(m_1\in\mathcal H_1(1,1)\).  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}\!\left(\frac12,\partial[0,1]\right)
 =\frac12\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad
 f_{1t\mid z_0}(x)=1
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in[0,1].              \tag{13}
\]
The design dates are independent, so
\[
 \beta_1(k\mid z_0)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k\ge1.                                                 \tag{14}
\]

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T})\).  Training outcomes are
deterministic, and under \(\mathbb K_1\) unit \(i\)'s event history depends
only on \(\varepsilon_i\).  Mutual independence in (7) gives conditional
independence of unit histories across \(i\), while for \(r\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_r}[Q_{1ti}\mid\mathcal X]
 =\frac12=m_1(X_{1t}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_r}[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 =\frac12=\mu_1.                                                \tag{15}
\]
Taking expectations in the second equality shows for every \(i\) that
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_r}B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\frac12=\mu_{11}(z_0),                                       \tag{16}
\]
which is the common treated-replica mean required by the strengthened
\texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}.  Equations (15)--(16) impose no
identical-distribution or within-unit training/event independence
condition.  Every \(X_{1t}\) is observed exactly.  The donor sigma-field is
generated by \((\eta_j)_j\), while the joint panel is generated by
\((X_{1t})_t\) and, under \(\mathbb K_1\), \((\varepsilon_i)_i\).  Thus
(7) also proves donor independence from the entire joint panel.

The donor conditions follow from (8):
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_r}Z_j=z_0=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_r}(Z_j)=1=\Sigma,
 \qquad
 c_\Sigma I_1\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_1,               \tag{17}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_r}
 |\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4
 =\mathbb E|\eta_j|^4=1=B^4.                                  \tag{18}
\]
The positive lower eigenvalue in (17) justifies \(\Sigma^{-1/2}\).
Finally, (9) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_r}B_{1i}(0)=\frac12=m_1(z_0),            \tag{19}
\]
which is event-date transport, and (10) gives consistency.  Equations
(8)--(19) verify every clause of Definition
\texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}.  Therefore
\[
 \xi^{(0)},\xi^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(z_0).            \tag{20}
\]
If the query variable equals \(1/2\) almost surely and its conditional
causal-data kernel is \(\mathbb K_r\), then (13)--(19), now read
conditionally on the sole query value, verify every member property of
Definition \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, including the common-mean clause
of \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}.  Hence
\[
 P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)},                     \tag{21}
\]
without selecting a conditional version at a null query.

The joint law of \(((X_{1t})_t,(Q_{1ti})_{t,i},(Z_j)_j)\) is common to
\(\mathbb K_0\) and \(\mathbb K_1\) by (7)--(8).  By Definition
\texttt{def:target}, (9)--(10), and \(\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \tau_{\mathbb K_0}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_0}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)]=0,\\
 \tau_{\mathbb K_1}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_1}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)]
 =\frac14\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0.
 \end{aligned}                                                  \tag{22}
\]
Nevertheless, (10) and independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from
\(\mathcal X\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_0}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_1}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)
 =\frac1{16}\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i)=\frac1{16}.     \tag{23}
\]
Thus the repaired centered class still permits distinct event-noise
constants while holding the training experiment, donor experiment, and
causal target fixed.  This is the claimed explicit certificate.

Put
\[
 p_E=\mathbb K_\xi(E),
 \qquad
 \mu_s=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}].
\]
Membership in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), bounded wealth, and
consistency imply \(|B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}|\le B\) almost surely, so the
displayed expectation and all following conditional expectations exist.
Since \(E\in\mathcal X\), the assumed equality
\(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b\mathbf 1_E\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 =b\mathbf 1_E
 \quad\mathbb K_\xi\text{-almost surely}.                     \tag{1}
\]
The design-conditional-centering clause in Definition
\texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} gives instead
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 =\mu_s
 \quad\mathbb K_\xi\text{-almost surely}.                     \tag{2}
\]
Taking expectations in the assumed shock representation and using the
definition of \(\mu_s\) gives
\[
 \mu_s=b\,\mathbb K_\xi(E)=bp_E.                               \tag{3}
\]
Equations (1)--(3), followed by squaring and integration, imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 0
 &=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[(b\mathbf 1_E-bp_E)^2]\\
 &=b^2\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[(\mathbf 1_E-p_E)^2]\\
 &=b^2p_E(1-p_E),
 \end{aligned}                                                  \tag{4}
\]
where the last equality uses \(\mathbf 1_E^2=\mathbf 1_E\).  Since
\(b\ne0\), division by \(b^2>0\) in (4) gives
\(p_E(1-p_E)=0\).  Because \(p_E\in[0,1]\), this is equivalent to
\(p_E\in\{0,1\}\).

For the scalar observable law in the statement, the uniform design and
\(q\in(0,1)\) give
\[
 \mathbb K_\xi(E)
 =\mathbb K_\xi(X_{11}\le q)=q\in(0,1).
\]
Taking \(b=b_*>0\) contradicts (4), irrespective of the nuisance labels.
Thus no such labelled point satisfies design-conditional centering, so none
belongs to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Event-date transport,
temporal mixing, and donor conditions are not used.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) and a regular conditional law
\(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}=P(\,\cdot\mid z_0)\).  For every cohort set
\[
 \mu_{P,s}(z_0)=\mu_{1s}(z_0),
 \qquad
 \Sigma_P(z_0)=\operatorname{Var}_P(Z_j\mid z_0),               \tag{1}
\]
and retain the panel-law regression labels \(m=(m_1,\ldots,m_S)\).
Bounded wealth makes every treated conditional mean in (1) finite.  We
verify all clauses of Definition \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} on
one marginal-conull set of query values.

The common treated-mean equality in Assumption
\texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} gives, for every replica \(i\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]
 =\mu_{1s}(z_0)=\mu_{P,s}(z_0).                                \tag{2}
\]
The equality is common across \(i\), but it asserts neither identical
distributions nor independence between a unit's training and event
outcomes.  Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency} disintegrates to
\(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\) almost surely under the kernel, while
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-date-transport} gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_{0s}).            \tag{3}
\]
Thus (2)--(3) verify the common label, consistency, and transport clauses.

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{u,v})\).  The two equalities in
Assumption \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, interpreted under a
regular conditional law at \(z_0\), give
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}[Q_{sti}\mid\mathcal X]
 =m_s(X_{st}),                                                  \tag{4}
\]
and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}
 [B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 &=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]\\
 &=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]\\
 &=\mu_{P,s}(z_0),
 \end{aligned}                                                  \tag{5}
\]
where the last equality is (2).  Equations (4)--(5) use only conditional
mean restrictions; they add no response-calendar mixing or within-unit
independence.

The almost-sure boundedness, exact-design observation, and interior
conditions under \(P\) disintegrate to the corresponding
\(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}\)-almost-sure conditions outside a marginally null set.
The Holder condition is a property of the labelled functions \(m_s\) and
is unchanged by conditioning.  Assumption \texttt{ass:design-density}
supplies, for every \(s,t\),
\[
 c_X\le f_{st\mid z_0}(x)\le C_X
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in[0,1]^d,             \tag{6}
\]
and Assumption \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing} supplies
\[
 \beta_s(k\mid z_0)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k\ge1,                                                 \tag{7}
\]
for almost every query.  Assumption \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence},
which conditions on both \(z_0\) and \(\mathcal X\), becomes conditional
independence of the unit histories given \(\mathcal X\) under the fixed
kernel.  No stronger factorization is used.

Likewise, Assumptions \texttt{ass:donor-independence} and
\texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} are conditional factorization
statements and therefore give, under \(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}\), independent
and identically distributed donors independent of the entire joint panel.
Assumptions \texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness},
\texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}, and
\texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}, together with (1), give
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}Z_j=z_0,
 \qquad
 c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma_P(z_0)\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}, \tag{8}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}
 \left[\|\Sigma_P(z_0)^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\right]
 \le B^4.                                                       \tag{9}
\]
The lower eigenvalue bound \(c_\Sigma>0\) in (8) makes the inverse square
root in (9) well defined.

There are finitely many cohorts, dates, and replicas and only countably many
lags \(k\).  Intersecting the conull query sets on which (2)--(9) and the
disintegrated support conditions hold therefore leaves a marginal-conull
set.  At each query in this intersection, the labelled point
\[
 \xi_P(z_0)=\bigl(\mathbb K_{P,z_0};\mu_P(z_0),m,\Sigma_P(z_0)\bigr)
\]
satisfies every member property of
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  This proves the assertion and makes
no statement about an arbitrarily chosen conditional version on the
complementary null set.

proposed.condition:
With \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{1\le u\le S,\ 1\le v\le T})\), every \(s,t,i\) satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{st})
\]
and every \(s,i\) satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]
 =\mu_{1s}(z_0)
\]
almost surely.

standard.name: conditional mean centering with a common within-cohort treated mean

proposed_core_edits.reason: The previous centering condition made each treated outcome invariant to the design after conditioning on the query, but did not state that its query-conditional mean is common across replicas.  The added equality supplies exactly that missing transfer premise without imposing identical distributions, within-unit training/event independence, or response-calendar mixing.

proposed.name: \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\)
proposed.construction:
Fix a deterministic query
\(z_0=(z_{01}^{\top},\ldots,z_{0S}^{\top})^{\top}\in([0,1]^d)^S\), and let
\[
 \mathcal O=\sigma\bigl((X_{st})_{s,t},(Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},
 (B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i},(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}\bigr)
\]
be the common observable sigma-field.  Define
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) to be the class of labelled parameter points
\[
 \xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma),
 \qquad \mu=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_S),
 \qquad m=(m_1,\ldots,m_S),                                    \tag{1}
\]
where \(\mathbb K_\xi\) is a causal-data kernel at the fixed query whose observable restriction is a probability law on \(\mathcal O\), and
\[
 \mu_s=\mu_{1s}(z_0)
 =\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}]
 \quad\text{for every }i.                                      \tag{2}
\]
The following pointwise clauses are imposed.  First, for every \(s,i\),
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(z_{0s},\partial[0,1]^d)\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\ \mathbb K_\xi\text{-almost surely},
 \qquad \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_{0s}),       \tag{3}
\]
\(|Q_{sti}|\vee|B_{si}(0)|\vee|B_{si}(1)|\le B\) almost surely,
\(m_s\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), and every \(X_{st}\) is observed exactly.  Second, for every \(s,t\), \(X_{st}\) has a Lebesgue density \(f_{st\mid z_0}\) satisfying
\[
 c_X\le f_{st\mid z_0}(x)\le C_X
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in[0,1]^d,             \tag{4}
\]
and the sequence \((X_{st})_{t=1}^{T}\) has beta-mixing coefficients
\(\beta_s(k\mid z_0)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\) for every \(k\ge1\).  Third, with
\(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{u,v})\), unit histories are conditionally independent across \((s,i)\) given \(\mathcal X\), and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[Q_{sti}\mid\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]=\mu_s. \tag{5}
\]
Fourth, the donors are independent and identically distributed, are independent of the entire joint panel
\(((X_{st})_{s,t},(Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i})\), and satisfy
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}Z_j=z_0,
 \qquad \Sigma=\operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_\xi}(Z_j),
 \qquad c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd},  \tag{6}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\le B^4.                        \tag{7}
\]
Every estimator and random interval in an outer minimax, coverage, or expected-length display over the generated-query class is required to be \(\mathcal O\)-measurable and to be one rule selected before both the unknown donor mean \(z_0\) and the unknown labelled point \(\xi\).  Such a rule may not take \(z_0\), potential outcomes, or nuisance labels \((\mu,m,\Sigma)\) as inputs.  This outer convention differs from the deterministic experiment \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\), where the fixed specification \((X,z_0,\Sigma)\) is known before the rule is selected.  The outer convention retains the donor-location channel.  The class consists of labelled fixed-query points; it does not choose a regular conditional version for a panel law at a query-null value.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The replacement records the common treated-replica label explicitly and states the outer generated-query timing convention: one observable-data rule is chosen before the unknown donor mean and labelled point.

proposed.name: Deterministic induced fixed-design product experiment
proposed.construction:
Fix a deterministic array \(X=(X_{st})_{1\le s\le S,1\le t\le T}\), an interior reference path \(z_0\), and \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S_{++}^{Sd}\).  The local deterministic product experiment \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) consists of labelled parameter points \(\xi=(\mathbb Q_\xi;\mu,f,z)\), where \(\mathbb Q_\xi\) is a law of
\[
 \mathcal O_X=\bigl((E_{si})_{s,i},(Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}\bigr)
\]
labelled by \((\mu,f,z)\), where \(\mu=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_S)\in[-B,B]^S\), every \(f_s\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) satisfies \(\|f_s\|_\infty\le B\), and
\[
 z\in([0,1]^d)^S,\qquad
 \operatorname{dist}(z_s,\partial[0,1]^d)\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(z-z_0)\|_2^2\le1.
\]
Under \(\mathbb Q_\xi\), \(|E_{si}|\vee|Q_{sti}|\le B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}E_{si}=\mu_s,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}Q_{sti}=f_s(X_{st}),
\]
the histories \(((E_{si},(Q_{sti})_{t=1}^{T}))_{s,i}\) are independent across \((s,i)\), with arbitrary dependence within a history, and the donor sample is independent of these histories and is independent and identically distributed with
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}Z_j=z,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb Q_\xi}(Z_j)=\Sigma,\qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z)\|_2^4\le B^4.
\]
The statistical target attached to \(\xi\) is
\[
 \theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)
 =\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mu_s-f_s(z_s)\}.
\]
For each fixed specification \((X,z_0,\Sigma)\), estimators in this experiment are measurable functions of \(\mathcal O_X\) together with the known deterministic inputs \((X,z_0,\Sigma)\).  The rule is selected before the unknown labelled point \(\xi\), cannot use the labels \((\mu,f,z)\), and may be indexed by the fixed specification; no single rule is required to work unchanged across distinct values of \((X,z_0,\Sigma)\).  This definition is a deterministic experiment for every \(X\); it does not select a version of a regular conditional distribution at a null design.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The deterministic experiment must allow its decision rule to depend on the known fixed specification \(X,z_0,\Sigma\), while requiring selection only before the unknown labelled parameter point.  This is distinct from the outer generated-query convention.

proposed.name: Fixed-query observed-law functional
proposed.construction:
For a labelled point
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), where the treated-replica mean is common and
\[
 \mu_s=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}]
 \quad\text{for every }i,
\]
define
\[
 \theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)
 =\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}.                   \tag{1}
\]
This is an observed-law functional on the common observable sigma-field.  Indeed, \(\mu_s\) is the common mean of the observed bounded treated-replica coordinates.  If \(m_s\) and \(m_s^\dagger\) are two Holder-continuous versions of
\(\mathbb E[Q_{sti}\mid X_{st}=x]\) under the same observed law, then they agree almost surely under the law of \(X_{st}\).  The lower density bound \(c_X>0\) implies that they agree Lebesgue-almost everywhere.  Their difference is continuous; if it were nonzero at any point, it would be bounded away from zero on a relative open ball of positive Lebesgue measure, a contradiction.  Thus
\(m_s=m_s^\dagger\) everywhere on \([0,1]^d\), in particular at \(z_{0s}\), so (1) is uniquely determined by the observed law.  This definition does not identify a causal target.  For a labelled causal kernel, equality with \(\tau(z_0)\) follows from Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and its consistency and event-date-transport clauses.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The observed-law functional must say that its treated-coordinate mean is common across every replica, matching the repaired centering condition and transfer lemma.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\), the common treated-replica label satisfies \(\mu_s=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) for every replica \(i\). Consistency, event-date transport, and the common-mean clause of design-conditional centering therefore identify \(\tau(z_0)=\sum_s\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}\) for every \(\mathbb P_{z_0}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\). For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the deterministic fixed-design experiment supplies the conditional optimal-recovery bound; at each fixed specification \(X,z_0,\Sigma\), its rule may use these known deterministic inputs and is selected only before the unknown labelled point. Random-design MSE and honest expected-length bounds and converses are uniform over the fixed-query generated-center class, where one observable-data rule is instead selected before the unknown donor mean \(z_0\) and labelled kernel. The marginal squared-risk scale is \(R_\star=R_{\mathrm{or}}\vee N^{-\lambda}\), with the independent-calendar spacing replacement on \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\). The feasible interval uses whole-unit concentration and no calendar-score branch. For every joint panel law, the strengthened centering condition and the other class assumptions imply that its regular conditional kernel belongs to the fixed-query class for almost every query, and only there do the causal risk and coverage conclusions transfer. No supremum is taken over panel-specific values of a regular conditional law at a null query, no lower local modulus is assumed, and no headline result is claimed for \(\lambda>1\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The estimand metadata must expose both the common treated-replica mean used by the repaired bridge and the different decision-rule timing in the deterministic fixed-design and outer generated-query experiments.
